related_questions.question: What does an STD do to a person?
related_questions.snippet: Sexually transmitted infections can cause lifelong complications if left untreated. Common complications from untreated STIs include the following: HIV can lead to AIDS. Syphilis can damage your organs, nervous system and infect a developing fetus.

related_questions.question: Can STD be cured?

text_blocks.snippet: An STD, or sexually transmitted disease, is an infection that is passed from one person to another through sexual contact. These infections can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites. While the term "STD" is often used interchangeably with "STI" (sexually transmitted infection), the term STI is becoming more common, as it encompasses infections that may not yet have developed into a full-blown disease.
snippet_highlighted_words: an infection that is passed from one person to another through sexual contact

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: STDs/STIs are primarily spread through sexual activity, including vaginal, anal, and oral sex.

list.title: Causes:
list.snippet: They can be caused by various pathogens:
Bacteria: Examples include chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis.
Viruses: Examples include HIV, herpes, HPV, and hepatitis B.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Some STDs/STIs have noticeable symptoms like genital sores, unusual discharge, or pain during urination. However, many infections can be asymptomatic, meaning the person has the infection but doesn't experience any symptoms.

list.title: Importance of Testing:
list.snippet: Because many STDs/STIs are asymptomatic, it's crucial to get tested regularly, especially if you're sexually active.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Some STDs/STIs are curable with antibiotics (bacterial infections), while others are manageable with antiviral medications (viral infections).

list.title: Public Health Importance:
list.snippet: STDs/STIs are a significant public health concern, with millions of new cases occurring each year.

list.title: Using the Terms:
list.snippet: While "STD" and "STI" are often used interchangeably, "STI" is becoming more common to reflect the fact that a person can have an infection without developing a disease.
